exposure: type of delivery (normal vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
outcome: thoracoabdominal mobility (thoracic area mobility, abdominal area mobility)
cohort: Newborns (n=26) of both sexes, 37-41 weeks gestational age, and up to 72 hours of life, born by normal delivery or cesarean section.
finding: The study found that the type of delivery influenced abdominal mobility and respiratory rate, with newborns delivered by cesarean section exhibiting lower abdominal mobility.
mod_finding: Newborns delivered by cesarean section presented lower abdominal mobility compared to those born by normal vaginal delivery.
